title: The Last Safehouse
premise: Odile Oyelaran, a crash investigator who lost their family in a disaster officially blamed on pilot error, has spent years living under an assumed name with a go-bag by the door. When Flight 4471 disappears from every radar, database, and memory mid-flight—except theirs—they realize the crash that killed their family was the first test of a technology that erases events from consensus reality. Hunted by the consortium behind it and aided by a ragged network of fellow 'unrecorded' survivors, Odile must decide whether to trade the one piece of evidence they've hidden for a decade—the black box from row twelve—for the lives of the safehouse family that has become their own. In the end, Odile broadcasts the truth to thousands of strangers at once, making the record too widespread to erase, at the cost of their own name vanishing from every file on earth.
about_author: Quentin Dravenmoor is the pen name of a former aviation safety analyst who left the industry after a report of theirs was quietly withdrawn from public record. They write thrillers about ordinary people trapped inside systems designed to forget them.

chapters.title: Row Twelve
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. On the tenth anniversary of the crash, Odile visits the memorial wall and touches the names of their family, then returns home to repack a go-bag no one knows about. Emotional beat: grief worn smooth into ritual, and the loneliness of a lie kept polished for ten years.

chapters.title: The Flight That Wasn't
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. Working late at the investigation bureau, Odile watches Flight 4471 vanish from live tracking mid-air; within hours, tickets, manifests, crew records—even coworkers' memories—show no such flight. Emotional beat: vertigo, the horror of doubting your own perception.

chapters.title: Consensus
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. Odile tests reality: photos on their phone, a survivor's voicemail, a scrap of fuselage in their locker—all gone or denied. Their supervisor gently suggests leave. Emotional beat: gaslit isolation, the first crack in Odile's careful invisibility.

chapters.title: The Go-Bag
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. Odile flees their apartment as unmarked cars circle the block, grabbing the bag packed for ten years. Inside is the black box recovered secretly from row twelve—their true inheritance. Emotional beat: terror fused with grim purpose; the lie finally has a use.

chapters.title: Safehouse
chapters.summary: Marisol's POV. Odile reaches a shuttered lighthouse hostel run by Marisol, a forger of identities, and its odd residents: a retired air marshal, a teenage hacker called Finch, and a mute former pilot. Emotional beat: wary shelter, the first unfamiliar warmth of found family.

chapters.title: Rules of the House
chapters.summary: Marisol's POV. Marisol explains the safehouse's purpose: protecting people the consortium has 'unwritten.' Odile hides the black box but can't bring themselves to say what it is. Emotional beat: belonging offered on condition of trust Odile isn't ready to give.

chapters.title: Finch Finds a Thread
chapters.summary: Finch's POV. Finch traces 4471's ghost data to Meridian Dynamics, a defense contractor whose 'Continuity' program edits recorded reality. Emotional beat: teenage triumph curdling into fear when the trace pings back.

chapters.title: The Man from Meridian
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. A courteous Meridian agent, Halloran, finds Odile and offers everything Odile ever wanted: official truth about row twelve, restored records, even an apology—in exchange for the black box. Emotional beat: temptation wearing a human face.

chapters.title: What Row Twelve Knows
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. Flashback chapter: the night of the original crash, young investigator Odile pocketing the recorder before it could be logged, sensing the official story was wrong. Emotional beat: guilt reframed as inheritance—the box is their family's last testimony.

chapters.title: Unwritten
chapters.summary: Retired air marshal Cole's POV. Cole reveals he was aboard 4471's sister flight and remembers being erased; he shows Odile his own fading photographs. Emotional beat: two witnesses recognizing each other across decades of silence.

chapters.title: The Price of Names
chapters.summary: Marisol's POV. Meridian raids a sister safehouse; refugees arrive with nothing, including residents whose families no longer remember them. Emotional beat: collective grief, and Marisol's quiet fury hardening into resolve.

chapters.title: Halloran's Second Offer
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. Halloran escalates: he'll restore Odile's dead family to every record, photograph, and memory—if Odile surrenders the box. Emotional beat: the cruelest temptation yet, grief weaponized against love.

chapters.title: Confession at the Table
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. At dinner, Odile finally tells the safehouse everything: row twelve, the box, the offers. Instead of exile, Finch takes their hand. Emotional beat: the lie breaking open into belonging.

chapters.title: Counterfeit Truths
chapters.summary: Finch's POV. The household plans a sting: feed Meridian a decoy box while Finch exfiltrates Continuity's master index. Emotional beat: fragile hope, a family building something together.

chapters.title: The Exchange
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. The handoff at a fogbound airfield goes wrong—Halloran knew, and Marisol is taken instead. Emotional beat: betrayal's cold shock; Odile's old instinct to run versus staying to fight.

chapters.title: What We Keep
chapters.summary: Cole's POV. Cole sacrifices himself covering the others' escape, passing Odile his own evidence—a lifetime of fading proof. Emotional beat: inheritance passed hand to hand; mourning without a grave.

chapters.title: Inside Continuity
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. Odile trades themselves to Meridian for Marisol, walking into headquarters carrying the real box. Emotional beat: calm resolve, a person finally done hiding.

chapters.title: The Erasure Room
chapters.summary: Halloran's POV. Halloran shows Odile the machine that unwrites events—and offers to erase Odile's grief itself. Odile refuses: the grief is the proof of love. Emotional beat: the villain's seduction failing against stubborn humanity.

chapters.title: Broadcast
chapters.summary: Finch's POV. From the safehouse, Finch hijacks Continuity's own distribution network while Odile triggers the box's playback inside Meridian—row twelve's final minutes streamed to millions before the system can react. Emotional beat: desperate, exhilarating defiance.

chapters.title: Too Many Witnesses
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. The truth spreads faster than it can be unwritten; Meridian's program collapses under the weight of shared memory. Halloran, facing exposure, offers one last trade. Emotional beat: vindication shadowed by cost.

chapters.title: The Name That Vanished
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. To seal the broadcast beyond reversal, Odile lets the machine take their records—their history, credentials, even their name—vanishing from every file on earth. Emotional beat: loss and liberation entwined; identity surrendered so truth survives.

chapters.title: Homecoming
chapters.summary: Marisol's POV. Weeks later, a stranger with familiar eyes arrives at the lighthouse door carrying nothing but a go-bag. The household sets another plate. Emotional beat: quiet joy—belonging that needs no records, a family that remembers for you.
